title: The Mirror Lake Tax
story: On the silver shore of Mirror Lake, a tall thin monster made of standing water demands a share of every traveler's cargo before letting them cross. Mr 6 arrives leading a raft carrying 480 moonstone shards meant for the village orphanage. Rhennadel ripples: "I take 35 percent, and then 20 percent of what remains — that is only fair to a reflection."
question: How many moonstone shards would the orphanage have left after both of Rhennadel's cuts?
solution: After the first cut of 35%, Mr 6 keeps 65%: 480 x 0.65 = 312 shards.
Rhennadel then takes 20% of THAT, so Mr 6 keeps 80%: 312 x 0.8 = 249.6 shards.
The orphanage would keep 249.6 shards — and Mr 6 points out the toll's own reflection owes the same, which cancels the whole debt.
praise: Working with percents in two stages is exactly right — the second percent has to be taken from the new smaller amount, not the original 480.
hint: After a 35% cut, what fraction of the shards is still on the raft? Take the second percent from that number, not from 480.
victory: Mr 6 tilts his shield so Rhennadel sees itself, and the reflection politely demands a toll from the toll — the puddle argues itself flat. The orphanage gets every shard.
imagePrompt: A tall watery humanoid toll-keeper standing on a glassy silver lake at dawn, mist curling, as a small heroic numeral-six knight in a blue cape angles a mirrored shield toward it.
